name: Bandar Seri Begawan Centre
tagline: The mosque, the river and the compact core
description: The small central district around the Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque and its lagoon, with the government offices, the Royal Regalia Museum and the waterfront where the water taxis leave. It is the only genuinely walkable part of the country.
bestFor: Short stays wanting the mosque and the water village at the door
pros: The mosque and its reflecting lagoon
cons: Almost nothing open in the evening

name: Kampong Ayer
tagline: The water village on stilts, still inhabited
description: A settlement of houses, schools, mosques and shops built on stilts over the Brunei River, continuously inhabited for centuries and still home to thousands of people. Water taxis cross to it from the centre in minutes for almost nothing.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to stay somewhere genuinely unlike anywhere else
pros: A living settlement rather than an exhibit
Water taxis run constantly and cost almost nothing
The cultural heart of the country
cons: Boardwalks and boats for all movement

name: Gadong
tagline: Where Brunei actually shops and eats
description: The commercial district a few kilometres from the centre, with the shopping malls, the supermarkets and the night market where most of the capital eats in the evening. It is unremarkable to look at and it is where daily life happens.
bestFor: Longer stays needing supermarkets, malls and the night market
pros: The night market is the best eating in Brunei
cons: A car or taxi is needed
Traffic on the main roads at peak

name: Jerudong and the Coast
tagline: The northwestern coast, with the beaches and the park
description: The coastal strip northwest of the capital, with Jerudong Park, the beaches at Muara and Empire, and the more expensive residential development. It is greener and quieter than the capital and where the country's coast is accessible.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a beach and space rather than the compact centre
pros: Greener and quieter than the centre
Jerudong Park and the coastal road

name: Temburong
tagline: The separated district, and the rainforest
description: Brunei's eastern district, physically cut off from the rest of the country by Malaysian territory and reached by a bridge opened in 2020 or by longboat. Ulu Temburong National Park protects primary rainforest with a canopy walkway into it.
bestFor: Anyone whose reason for coming is the forest
pros: Primary rainforest and the canopy walkway
The bridge has made it a day trip
cons: An hour or more from the capital
